Set operations on 1-D arrays

Source: R/numpy_setops.R
jnp_setops.Rd

Ports of jnp.union1d, jnp.intersect1d, jnp.setdiff1d, jnp.setxor1d and jnp.isin. Inputs are flattened. Without size the inputs must be concrete; with a static size the result has exactly size entries, padded with fill_value.

Usage

jnp_union1d(ar1, ar2, size = NULL, fill_value = NULL)

jnp_setdiff1d(ar1, ar2, assume_unique = FALSE, size = NULL, fill_value = NULL)

jnp_setxor1d(ar1, ar2, assume_unique = FALSE, size = NULL, fill_value = NULL)

jnp_intersect1d(
  ar1,
  ar2,
  assume_unique = FALSE,
  return_indices = FALSE,
  size = NULL,
  fill_value = NULL
)

jnp_isin(
  element,
  test_elements,
  assume_unique = FALSE,
  invert = FALSE,
  method = "auto"
)

Arguments

ar1, ar2

Arrays.

size

Optional static output size.

fill_value

Padding value when size exceeds the number of results.

assume_unique

Whether the inputs are known to have no repeated entries.

return_indices

intersect1d: also return the 0-based indices of the common values in ar1 and ar2.

element, test_elements

isin: test each entry of element for membership in test_elements.

invert

isin: return the negated result.

method

isin: "auto", "compare_all", "binary_search" or "sort".

Value

An array (intersect1d with return_indices = TRUE: a list of three arrays; isin: a boolean array of the shape of element).
